name: codon_aligner
short: Bio.Align.CodonAligner of Biopython 1.88: a protein aligned to its nucleotide sequence over the three translated frames with frame-shift scores (-2, -1, +1, +2); score and every alignment as vertices (refuses the inputs on which Biopython's iterator reads uninitialised memory).
description: Bio.Align.CodonAligner of Biopython 1.88: the optimal score and every alignment of a protein and its nucleotide sequence (DNA or RNA) over the three translated frames, with scores for the frame shifts -2 / -1 / +1 / +2; see the tool description in the code for the parameters.

alignments: coordinates: the vertices (target = residues, query = nucleotides) of every alignment

errors: A codon has a letter outside IUPAC (Biopython: TranslationError)
Unknown genetic code table, or a wildcard that is not a single character
The reference iterator reads memory its traceback never wrote on this input (InvalidOperationException; scoreOnly = true still gives the score)

example.title: A frame shift between codon 7 and 8
example.prompt: Align this protein to its nucleotide sequence allowing frame shifts.
example.note: The query goes back by one nucleotide at the frame shift (21 -> 20): the codon of residue 8 overlaps the previous one by one nucleotide (Bio.Align doctest of CodonAligner.align).

name: multiple_seq_alignment
short: The legacy Bio.Align.MultipleSeqAlignment of Biopython 1.88: rows / columns / slices / add / sort / substitutions / alignment / append / extend / delete and the column annotations on an alignment of records.
description: One operation of the legacy Bio.Align.MultipleSeqAlignment of Biopython 1.88 (summary, length, alignment_length, row, rows, row_columns, cell, column, slice, add, sort, substitutions, alignment, append, extend, delete_row, delete_rows, column_annotations, set_column_annotation) on an alignment of records; see the tool description in the code for the parameters.

resultJson: The value as JSON: an alignment {records, annotations, column_annotations}, a record, a string, a number or a matrix {letters, values}
text: str(alignment) when the value is an alignment

errors: Sequences must all be the same length
list index out of range / index out of range (a row or a column that does not exist)
Any per-letter annotation should be a Python sequence (list, tuple or string) of the same length as the biological sequence, here N.
When adding two alignments they must have the same length (i.e. same number of rows)

example.title: A sub-alignment of rows 1-4 and columns 3-5
example.prompt: Take rows 1 to 4 and columns 3 to 5 of this alignment.
